packages.label: גְּבוּרוֹת וּרְעָמִים
packages.reason: All these nodes share the same essential nature: the divine powers of severity (gevurot) that, when combined with love and directed through the throat (kaneh), produce thunder — the powerful voice of prayer that strikes the skull and illumines the mochin. שם אג״לא is the divine name of gevurot; גילדנא shares the same letter-root; כח וגבורה שאדם מוציא הקול בכח and קול שאדם מוציא בכח בתפלתו are the experiential and functional equivalents of re'amim; הרעים is an alternative verbal form of רעמים. The kaneh (throat-pipe) is the physical conduit through which the powerful voice (re'amim) exits.
nodes: כח וגבורה, שאדם מוציא את הקול בכח גדול

merge_notes.reason: The kaneh (throat-reed) is defined as the bechina of the voice issuing from it — a structural/instrumental definition that places it in the same domain as re'amim and gevurot. The Torah teaches that the powerful voice of prayer passes through the kaneh and becomes thunder; קנה and its voice are therefore two faces of the same reality as gevurot/re'amim.

packages.label: יִרְאָה וַחֲשִׁיבוּת
packages.reason: These nodes share the essential nature of holy fear (yirat Hashem), which is the same as genuine dignity/importance (chashivut). Yirah is described explicitly as gevurah and chashivut — fear of Heaven is the treasury of true honor. אשה (the feminine) is the bechina of yirah (the receptive, inward quality). הרים (mountains) are the bechina of tzaddikim — the ones who embody genuine yirat Hashem and thus carry real chashivut. All express the inward dimension of holy awe.

merge_notes.reason: The proof text 'הרים בחינת צדיקים' establishes that mountains = tzaddikim. In the context of Torah #5 (LM2), the tzaddikim are the 'maginnei eretz' (shields of the earth) whose genuine yirat Hashem gives them true chashivut. Mountains carry the same qualities of stability, elevation, and genuine greatness that characterize yirah and chashivut — they are two faces of the same lofty, grounded quality. Merging with Package 2 (yirah/chashivut) rather than treating as a stand-alone pair.

packages.label: יִרְאָה חִיצוֹנִית וְסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא דִּגְבוּרָה
packages.label_en: External Fear and the Evil Side of Gevurah
packages.reason: These three nodes all share the essential nature of the external, corrupt dimension of gevurot. The Torah explicitly calls the chain of gevurot that descend without being sweetened with love 'yirah chitzonit' (external fear), and the Aramaic name for this is 'suspita d'dahava' (golden chip). They represent the evil counterpart of Package 1 (gevurot/re'amim) — when gevurot are not mixed with chasadim they become a klipa that blocks the voice from being heard.

packages.label: מֹחִין וּמַצָּה
packages.reason: All these nodes share the essential nature of pure, open intellect (mochin). Matzah = mochin (pure dough, unyeasted = unblocked mind). 'Be'avei mitra' (thick rain clouds) = mochin because the mochin drip down drop by drop like rain from above. 'Mei merivah' (waters of dispute) = matzah = mochin (via the Psalms verse about hidden thunder and Mei Merivah). Sheshet yemei hamaaseh = maaseh hamitzvot, because the practical mitzvot (physical action) are the vessel for constructing the mochin from below. Shabbat = joy of the world to come = the state of perfected mochin (olam haba is the eternal shabbat of illumined consciousness). All are expressions of the same pure, rectified intellect that the Torah instructs us to build.

merge_notes.reason: The proof text 'שישת ימי המעשה שהן בחינת מעשה המצוות שבהם נבראו עולם שנה נפש' equates the six working days with the practical mitzvot. In the Torah's argument, practical action (maaseh) is what draws down the mochin from above into the vessels below. The pair belongs with mochin/matzah since both represent the practical, physical dimension through which the pure intellect is constructed and maintained.

The proof text 'שמחת ותענוג עולם הבא שהוא בחינת שבת' makes these two directly equivalent. In the Torah's argument, simcha (joy) strengthens the malach (angel), which in turn protects the mochin/tefillin complex. Shabbat is the culminating state of perfect mochin — the complete rectification of intellect that the entire Torah is building toward. It belongs in the mochin cluster as the perfected state.

packages.label: סִטְרָא דְּמוֹתָא וְחָמֵץ
packages.label_en: The Side of Death and Chametz
packages.reason: Chametz (leavened bread, swollen dough) and sitra de-muta (the side of death) share the same essential nature: the impure, blocked intellect — the foreign wisdoms and evil thoughts that clog the brain like fermenting dough. Evil thoughts (hirhurim ra'im) are explicitly the 'kaneh destra achra' — the evil pipe/throat through which impurity flows into the mochin. This is the evil mirror of Package 4 (mochin/matzah).

merge_notes.reason: The proof text 'שלא תהרהר בהרהורים רעים שהם בחינת קנה דסטרא אחרא' defines evil thoughts as the evil throat-pipe. This is the direct functional counterpart of the holy kaneh in Package 1. In the sitra achra, evil thoughts flow through the kaneh destra achra into the mochin, blocking them with chametz (impure, foreign thoughts). Merged into Package 5 because hirhurim ra'im and kaneh destra achra are two faces of the same reality as sitra de-muta/chametz: the corruption and blocking of the intellect.

packages.label: אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה
packages.reason: These two nodes share the same essential nature: the highest level of prophetic clarity. 'Zeh hadavar' (this is the thing) is the language Moses uses — direct, unmediated, the clear mirror of prophecy. The Torah uses this as a positive touchstone for the level of direct apprehension of divine will. Both nodes express the same reality of unobstructed prophetic sight.

packages.label: כֹּה וְאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְאִירָה
packages.label_en: Koh and the Dim Mirror / Indirect Prophetic Sight
packages.reason: These nodes share the essential nature of indirect, incomplete perception of God. 'Koh' (thus/so) is the word used by other prophets who see from afar, through the dim mirror. The person who does mitzvot for their reward sees God only from a distance — they experience 'koh' rather than 'zeh.' This is a structural category (prophetic level) that can be good or deficient depending on context. Package 7 is the dim mirror that corresponds to Package 6 (the luminous mirror) — together they form the good/incomplete prophetic duality that runs through the Torah.
nodes: אדם העושה המצוה בשכר עולם הבא, שאינו נהנה מהמצוה בעצמה, אלו לא היו נותנין לו עולם הבא בשכרה, לא היה עושה אותה

packages.label: אַהֲבָה וָחֶסֶד
packages.reason: Ahavah (love) is bechina of 'ish' (the active male principle — the outpouring, giving dimension). Chesed is the quality of giving and revealing hidden things — the parsha (archer) who draws out and brings to light. All three (ahavah, ish, chesed/parsha) are two-faces of the same reality: the outpouring, revealing force of holy love. The Torah teaches that love must be combined with yirah (Package 2) to produce thunder (Package 1). Chesed (ahavah) is the counterpart to gevurot — they must be blended.

merge_notes.reason: The proof text 'פרשא דא בחינת חסד שהוא מוציא לאור תעלומות' establishes that the force of the archer/shooter is chesed because chesed reveals what is hidden. In the context of Torah #5 (LM2), chesed is the counterpart to gevurot — the Rebbe explicitly teaches that the gevurot (re'amim/thunder) must be accompanied by ahavah/chesed to reach the kavod (wisdom). Chesed/parsha shares the essential nature of ahavah/ish — all are the outpouring, revealing, active force of love.
